course_title: Advanced Therapy Skills: Working with Families and Groups
course_description:
This course will focus on the knowledge and skills required to work with families and to provide group therapy. The course will critically engage with theoretical frameworks, core principles and shared approaches of family and group therapies with an emphasis on how they are applied to diverse populations. Family and group engagement, clinical skills including assessment and treatment planning will be emphasised.

Welcome to PXMH7106

This course will focus on the knowledge and skills required to work with families and groups. Whether you have experience in these areas or are exploring them for the first time, there will be opportunities for you to expand your knowledge and skills.

course_aims: To establish student knowledge and skills of the history, frameworks and applications of group and family work.ﾠ

learning_outcomes.description: Critically evaluate the different approaches offered in clinical psychotherapy and/or art therapy family and group work literature and identify people and populations who may benefit.
Demonstrate awareness of family and group therapy’s underpinning philosophies and theoretical constructs and how they have shaped practice.
Apply understanding of family and group therapy approaches to develop appropriate interventions for a specific population.

assessment_details.title: Reflective Journal
assessment_details.due_date: 27/07/2026 - 31/10/2026 8 Journal entries, submitted by the Sunday of the chosen week.
assessment_details.task_description: Type: Journal Weight: 30% Task Description: Over the course of the semester students are expected to complete 8 journal entries, 300 words +/- 10%. Art Therapy journal entries include a visual reflection (1-2 images per entry). Each journal entry is to be completed by the Sunday after the selected tutorial, as response and analysis of the tutorial readings and discussion, and should include the following: Key aspects of the literature that stood out to you How the frameworks/interventions discussed resonate with you and your practice The final inclusion differs per area of speciality: Art Therapy: what the art work created conveys (and how), and how does it support your learning Psychotherapy: Any ethical or cultural consideration the content raised for you The student must post their journal reflection on blackboard. Criteria & Marking (Art Therapy): 1. Journal entries are original and show evidence that the reading and class discussion has been analysed and responded to in a thoughtful and reflective manner. 2. The prompting journal questions have been considered and responded to appropriately. 3. Art work is clearly presented and the quality of media, process of art making, and visual reflection is described. 4. There are 8 journal entries that are on time, are within the word limit, are free of spelling and grammatical errors, and which demonstrate appropriate care with the task. Criteria & Marking (Psychotherapy): 1. Journal entries are original and show evidence that the reading and discussion has been analysed and responded to in a thoughtful and reflective manner i.e. consideration of any cultural or ethical issues, and/ or integrating theory with clinical examples from practice where possible or appropriate. 2. The prompting journal questions have been considered and responded to appropriately 3. There are 8 journal entries that are on time, within the word limit, free of spelling and grammatical errors, and which demonstrate appropriate care with the task. assessment_details.title: Family Intervention Essay
assessment_details.task_description: Type: Essay Learning Objectives Assessed: 1, 2, 3, 4 Word Count: 2000 +/- 10% Task Description: Discuss a therapeutic intervention for a family - outlining theoretical frameworks and why you have used the application for this particular client group. Art Therapy students must include family art therapy interventions. Students are required to identify and discuss a population which could benefit from family therapy intervention. Students are required to describe the population, articulate their needs, explain how family [art] therapy could be beneficial, and identify family therapy strategies which may benefit the population. Assertions about the population and their needs must be backed up by reference to a range of sources including: recent literature, personal investigation and clinical or placement experience if relevant. Criteria & Marking: 1. Student has identified an appropriate population who could benefit from a family [art] therapy intervention. The population is described and their needs and challenges are articulated. 2. The reason family [art] therapy could be beneficial, including the choice of family strategies and intervention is articulated, and supported by literature. 3. Essay is in an appropriate academic form and structure, is well written and free from grammatical and spelling errors. Referencing and citation uses standard format and the essay is 2000 words (+/- 10%). Read full task description Hide full task description

assessment_details.title: Group Intervention and discussion ART THERAPY
assessment_details.task_description: Proposal Submission: Identify your co-facilitator and the chosen population. Email a proposal for your workshop to the Course Coordinator by Monday, October 5th. Workshop Preparation and Facilitation: Prepare and co-facilitate a therapy group with fellow students participating in a role-play. Identify a population that could benefit from group therapy and develop a suitable intervention. Ensure the intervention is informed by literature on the suitability and effectiveness for the chosen population. Demonstrate a high level of knowledge about the art media and skill in managing the group process. The activity should last 60-75 minutes and be suitable for the available facilities. Manage your time effectively. Feedback Session: Following the group, participate in a 15-minute feedback session where you will explain the rationale for your chosen activities, reflect on the co-facilitation experience and receive feedback from your peers. Criteria & Marking: Group therapy intervention is suitable and likely to be effective for the selected population You demonstrate a high level of knowledge of the art media and organisation skills in planning the intervention You demonstrate a high level of skill in managing group process, including processing of the art work and clear communication The activity is completed within the time frame and is suitable for the facilities and resources offered You demonstrate the ability to effectively co-facilitate a therapy group with a peer You are able to discuss the rationale for your work and critically reflect upon the process in a 15 minute feedback session. Following UQ guidelines, this assessment will marked against a rubric available to students, and it will be recorded for eventual review purposes. assessment_details.title: Presentation Group Therapy Proposal PSYCHOTHERAPY
assessment_details.other_conditions: Student specific, Secure. See the conditions definitions
assessment_details.task_description: Task Description: Prepare and deliver a 20-minute oral presentation proposing a group therapy intervention relevant to your current professional context or area of interest, including a short demonstration of a chosen intervention. Presentation Requirements: Target Population Identify and justify a specific population that would benefit from a group therapy approach. Group Intervention/ Activities Develop an appropriate group intervention tailored to the needs of the chosen population, and demonstrate a brief example of an intervention strategy to the group. Your proposal must be grounded in current literature, demonstrating an understanding of the therapeutic needs, strengths, and potential challenges associated with the group. Evidence Base Provide a clear rationale for your proposed group therapy model. Draw on contemporary research and relevant theoretical frameworks to justify the suitability and effectiveness of your intervention for the identified population. Group Structure and Process Explain the format and structure of your proposed group (e.g., open vs. closed, session frequency, facilitation style, therapeutic approach). Support your decisions with literature that outlines best practices in group facilitation and therapeutic outcomes. Discussion Component Following your presentation, you will participate in a 15-minute discussion facilitated by the Course Coordinator and fellow students. This is an opportunity to respond to questions, clarify your approach, and reflect on feedback. Presentation Dates Student presentations will be scheduled during the tutorial sessions on Thursday 22nd and 29th October 2026 . A schedule will be distributed in advance. Following UQ guidelines, this assessment will marked against a rubric available to students, and it will be recorded for eventual review purposes.
